cues.text: Simulated model, assumed signs. The foreleg brush is keyframed by hand; the spiking brain model is driven at antennal mechanosensory (Johnston's organ) neurons.
Simulated model: the Johnston's organ input lands in the AMMC, the antenna's vibration, wind and touch center.
Simulated model: the signal spreads to the inferior clamps and wedge, where descending neurons gather commands.
Simulated model: the gnathal ganglia, which run mouthpart and head muscles, join as the head dips toward the brushing leg.
Simulated model: the prow, a premotor shelf, routes the pattern toward descending neurons bound for leg motor circuits.
Simulated model: the keyframed leg keeps brushing; each spike remains a model guess, never a recording.
Simulated model: the sweep ends and the simulated antennal activity fades back to baseline.

qa.a: No — this clip is keyframed by hand. Only walking and escape replay recorded kinematics.
Antennal mechanosensory neurons of Johnston's organ — matching the antennal-grooming experiments of Shiu et al. 2024.
It processes the antenna's mechanical senses — vibration, wind, gravity and touch — the signals a brushing foreleg produces.
No. All spikes are simulated by the Shiu et al. 2024 model with partly assumed neurotransmitter signs; nothing was measured from a real fly.
